title: Relative coherent limit and colimit diagrams
statement:
Work in the fixed sufficiently large universes, with simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, right-pinched mapping spaces, and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The functor simplicial sets with quasicategory target are quasicategories, and their mapping simplicial sets are Kan complexes, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus].

For simplicial sets $A,B$, give each its formal degree $-1$ set $A_{-1}=B_{-1}=\{*\}$, with the unique augmentation. Define the join degreewise by
$$(A\star B)_n=\coprod_{\substack{i,j\geq-1\\ i+j+1=n}}A_i\times B_j\qquad(n\geq0).$$
A summand has an initial block of $i+1$ vertices from $A$ and a final block of $j+1$ vertices from $B$. A monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ acts by taking the inverse images of these two blocks and applying the simplicial operators to the resulting initial and final blocks; an empty block uses the unique degree $-1$ element. This specifies faces and degeneracies, including the pure-factor simplices. For a small simplicial set $K$, put $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$ and $K^{\triangleleft}=\Delta^0\star K$, with their pure-factor inclusions of $K$.

For clarity, for any strictly commutative square of Kan complexes
$$\begin{array}{ccc}A&\xrightarrow{f}&B\\ g\downarrow&&\downarrow h\\ C&\xrightarrow{k}&D,\end{array}$$
its path pullback model is
$$P=B\times_{D,h,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D,k}C.$$
An $n$-simplex of $P$ is $(b,c,\gamma)$ with $b\in B_n$, $c\in C_n$ and $\gamma:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to D$ whose endpoints are $h(b)$ and $k(c)$; all simplicial operators restrict these data. Call the square a homotopy pullback if the simplicial map $A\to P$ sending $a$ to $(f(a),g(a),\text{the constant interval at }hf(a)=kg(a))$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

Fix a functor $p:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ of quasicategories. For a diagram $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$, call $q$ a $p$-colimit diagram when, for every diagram $t:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$, the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal D)}(q,t)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}(q|_K,t|_K)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal B)}(pq,pt)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(pq|_K,pt|_K)
\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback, the horizontal maps being restriction and the vertical maps postcomposition by $p$. For $q:K^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal D$, the term $p$-limit diagram is defined by the same square with $(t,q)$ in place of $(q,t)$ and $K^{\triangleleft}$ in place of $K^{\triangleright}$. No existence of such diagrams is part of this definition.

lean.note: The join, terminal augmentation, pure-factor inclusions and path pullback reuse the existing landed constructions. Helpers construct the canonical constant-path comparison and its weak-equivalence predicate. Both relative predicates quantify over every comparison diagram, using outgoing mapping spaces for colimits and incoming mapping spaces for limits. The three added statement dependencies already have landed Lean records; no existing node is restated or repaired.
